question: Should OpenClaw publish requester-scoped MCP connections as a plugin SDK contract with a five-minute credential revalidation window, shared-session transcript visibility, and either replacement or fail-closed duplicate resolver ownership?
rationale: The implementation can be reviewed mechanically, but the permanent public API, credential revocation SLA, shared-conversation disclosure model, and cross-plugin ownership rule require explicit maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve with fail-closed ownership
options.body: Rebase the PR, reject duplicate server resolver registrations across plugins, retain the documented five-minute revalidation SLA, and land after renewed current-main proof.

options.title: Approve current replacement semantics
options.body: Rebase and land with last-registration-wins, explicitly documenting that plugin load order may replace resolver ownership for a server name.

options.title: Defer the public API
options.body: Keep the paired issue open while designing requester identity and authorization context together with cron, subagent, and broader MCP scoping work.

recommendation.title: Approve with fail-closed ownership
recommendation.body: Rebase the PR, reject duplicate server resolver registrations across plugins, retain the documented five-minute revalidation SLA, and land after renewed current-main proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal is ownership of the session MCP runtime and tests whose lifecycle and cache keys this API changes.
